Protects wallet users from an abort during keypool top-up that leaves a corrupted, inverted descriptor range on disk.

why: P1 because it fixes a reproducible node abort (assertion failure) triggered by a plausible RPC call, and the descriptor is written to disk before the crash, corrupting wallet state (author, molnard testing).
Also fixes a related undefined-behavior integer overflow in keypool top-up reachable without any import.
Related overflow work (#36245, #34861 discussion) shows this area has recurring correctness issues that this PR helps stabilize.

result.summary: Fixes a node crash in the wallet's descriptor import and keypool top-up code: WalletDescriptor stores its range in int32_t with an exclusive end, but the code that computes that end uses int64_t/unsigned arithmetic with no bound check, so an inclusive range endpoint of 2^31-1 (accepted by the shared descriptor-range parser) truncates to INT32_MIN. This aborts the node via an assertion in TopUpWithDB, and the same crash occurs with no explicit range at all when -keypool exceeds INT32_MAX. The PR adds bounds checks in ProcessDescriptorImport and TopUpWithDB, and adds functional test coverage for both crash paths plus a related integer-overflow case in keypoolrefill.
result.problem: Users importing a watch-only descriptor with a range ending at 2^31-1, or running with an oversized -keypool value, crash their node with an assertion failure, and the malformed descriptor is persisted to the wallet database before the crash, corrupting its on-disk range.

resolved_concerns: jeanpablojp asked for test coverage of the keypoolrefill overflow path; author added it in a force push.
molnard suggested a minor readability tweak to the new_range_end line; not blocking.

molnard raised several follow-up ideas (recovering already-corrupted descriptors, centralizing -keypool validation, changing TopUpWithDB's return semantics); author gave detailed responses and molnard agreed these are separate follow-ups that don't block this fix.

This is a reliability/fund-safety-adjacent issue: a corrupted descriptor range on disk affects the wallet's integrity, and the crash itself is a denial-of-service against the node's own operator. The fix also resolves a related integer-overflow UB in the keypoolrefill path reachable without any import.

result.card: This PR fixes a reproducible node crash: importing a watch-only descriptor with a range ending at 2^31-1, or running with -keypool above INT32_MAX, causes an assertion failure in TopUpWithDB because WalletDescriptor's int32_t range_end silently truncates and inverts, and the corrupted descriptor is written to disk before the abort. It also fixes a related integer-overflow (UB) in keypool top-up reachable via keypoolrefill without any import. Two contributors (molnard, kriss39) reproduced the crash on master and confirmed the fix works, giving tested ACKs, with additional concept ACKs and only non-blocking follow-up suggestions (deferred by consensus). The PR needs a rebase due to conflicts with several other open wallet PRs touching the same descriptor/keypool code (#36245, #36236, #35444, #35377, #34861), but the code itself is well reviewed. This is a P1 wallet reliability fix: a crash plus on-disk state corruption reachable from ordinary RPC usage.
